content.content:
A listed id whose other edge end names no node document — the entry rusopkql keeps in its place among its siblings in one of the detail panel's four relationship sections — has its id text drawn in the muted secondary colour role. That role is what mnwxnyks records under the colour-role aspect at its default state: the value muted, carried by --vscode-descriptionForeground, and the entry spends it as a role rather than as a property of one element — its id text is secondary text in its section, so the value the record fixes for secondary text is the value applied, through the token the record names. Nothing is substituted for that value, the role is not bound to a different colour, and no subject is attached to it beyond secondary text. The commitment is the colour role of that one entry's id text: which entry it is, what text it shows, and what activating it does are not changed by it.

The entry stays where it was. It is not dropped from its section, filtered out of the list, merged with a neighbour or replaced by stand-in text; its text is still the bare id it showed before, neither shortened nor relabelled, and no em dash, badge, tooltip or substitute control stands in for it. The mute is applied to that text and adds nothing to the entry beside it: the entry still sits among the entries of its section, still shows which id the selected node's field names, and still reads in the same lettering as its neighbours. Because the role is the secondary one as mnwxnyks records it — text that recedes without vanishing — the id stays legible: the entry's weight in the section is what changes, not its content, its place or its legibility.

The mute is a colour role and carries no claim of its own. It is not a fault, an error or a warning; it does not report that the panel is broken or incomplete, and it does not say the entry was meant to lead somewhere and failed. The entry is not followed here — the id it shows names no node document, so there is nowhere in the viewer to go (rusopkql) — and secondary text is the weight such an entry takes in its section, not the message that makes it the different case. Nothing here gives the role a second subject, borrows the way the canvas marks an unresolved edge, uses a warning colour, or lets the faintness stand in for the entry's label. Applied as mnwxnyks records it, the role keeps its one meaning: this text is drawn quieter than the text around it and no different in kind.

mwwxxzyk puts a listed entry in the panel as a link rather than bare text and, for this case, expressly allows the entry that names no node document to be presented muted; this decision takes that allowance for the colour role only, and settles nothing further about how the entry reads — nothing here requires an entry that names a node and one that names none to look alike. rusopkql adds no style rule of its own and leaves the entry's styling to the appearance decisions, and what activating the entry does stays that decision's, neither restated nor narrowed here. What else the entry's look carries — its pointer behaviour, its hover and focus marking — is not decided here, and this decision neither presumes nor rules out any of those cues; the decisions that own them settle them. Nor does this decision add a class, a style property or a stylesheet rule: it states the colour role the stylesheet decisions apply to that entry's id text.
content.rationale:
Mute is the smallest appearance that can set this entry apart without becoming a mark. The entry is a listed id whose activation changes nothing (rusopkql), and that decision is explicit that the panel entry carries no mark of its own: the marking of an unresolved edge belongs where the edge is drawn, not to the id text. What is left for the appearance of this entry is weight, and secondary text is the register that says "quieter than the text around it" while leaving the id fully legible. mnwxnyks already records that register as a colour role bound to the workbench theme, so the entry can spend a value the graph has rather than a colour invented for the occasion; the page keeps one account of what secondary text looks like, and stays theme-following instead of hard-coding a grey that would break in a light theme.

The costly alternative is to let the mute mean that the id names nothing. It would give one colour role two subjects — secondary text in one place, a broken reference in another — and it would turn an ordinary recorded fact, a reference to an id no document carries, into a viewer fault, which is the reading rusopkql's reasoning rejects on the behaviour side (no selection change, no error, no fault) and which this decision has to keep true on the appearance side. A tooltip, a badge, an em dash or a disabled-looking control would say the same thing louder, and each would be a mark the panel entry is not supposed to carry; the id instead stays readable as an id, in its place, drawn quieter.

Stopping at the colour role is what keeps the entry's look owned by one decision at a time. Which element carries the role, which class names it, whether the entry shows a pointer cursor or a hover underline, and how it is marked under focus are facts a reviewer can point at in a stylesheet or a renderer; settled in prose here they would be restated or contradicted by the decisions that own them, and the entry would end up with two accounts of its own look. Leaving them open also leaves those decisions free to abstain, which is what lets this one stand as it should: the entry is still listed, its text is still the bare id, and the only thing that has changed is that its text is drawn in the secondary role the graph records.
